lanes.title: the export's memory and speed: the telemetry streamed, the lines encoded in parallel in order, the same bytes (D-090 DI4)
lanes.brief:
SCOPE (D-090 DI4; READING DI4-R1): this lane may change Sim.Ui/Export (the session export: its reading of the telemetry, its encode and its self-check) and the code that calls it (the close path and the --export-session command), with Sim.Ui.Tests. It may read, but not change, the telemetry writer and readers in Sim.Core/Observability. Nothing in Sim.Core/Kernel. No change to what the run record holds, to simulation state, to the world hash or to any golden; the workbook's bytes and its self-check stay unchanged (DI4-R1). No permanent project, no CI change, no merge, tag or release.

READ FIRST: docs/d090-test-battles-dr24-battalions-export-director-answers-2026-11-12.md (DI4, DI4-R1), D-086, docs/adr/adr-059-one-file-session-export.md with its amendment of 2026-11-12, docs/m6-plan/run-record-research-and-exit-2026-11.md (§4's measurements and methods, and P2 to P4), docs/m6-session-export/README.md and reports/H-RR.md; code Sim.Ui/Export/*, Sim.Ui/SessionClose.cs, and the export calls in UiSession and Program.

(1) P2, MEMORY. Read the telemetry as a stream from the file instead of whole into memory; the sha256 and the line reader both run over the stream. Lane RR expected a saving of about the log's size in peak memory (INFERRED: 356 MB at 1,630 turns): MEASURE it.

(2) P3, TIME. Encode and check the lines in parallel, in order. Each line's work is independent; the results are placed by index and written in order, so the output is the same bytes at every thread count and under every schedule. Sim.Ui sits outside the banned-constructs scan (ADR-009), so the proof is yours: say how the construct you use keeps order, and show byte identity at 1, 2 and 4 threads and under a deterministic shuffled work order (never System.Random).

(3) THE SAME BYTES, MEASURED (DI4-R1). Byte-identical workbooks (sha256) before and after, on the Director's 850-turn files (read-only: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-civDemo/54b82655-610f-500e-a185-8fae64bdd108/scratchpad/rr2/director-src; the repository copy docs/m6-plan/playtest-session-20261108-155547-a1/ holds the same session with its telemetry zipped) and on a 1,630-turn session (rebuild it by lane RR's documented method, run-record doc §4; its manifest, orders and trace are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-civDemo/54b82655-610f-500e-a185-8fae64bdd108/scratchpad/rr2/m1630-base/snapshot, read-only). Time and peak memory before and after, three runs each, headless (--export-session) and on the in-game close path, compared with lane RR's figures. Lane RR's P4 stays unneeded unless P2 and P3 fall short; say whether they did.

(4) TESTS AND CHECKS. The streaming reader equals the whole-file reader (the same lines and sha256, including a last line without a newline, and CRLF line ends); the ordered parallel encode equals the sequential one, byte for byte; the self-check still catches a corrupted line (with a mutant); a bound on peak memory if it can be made reliable. Tier 1, Tier 2, then full Tier 3 in your clone, every full suite under flock on the shared lock; bounded mutants with semantic kills; the doc-link check. The run-record document gains a dated section; draft ADR-059's amendment entry in the lane report (the orchestrator applies it at integration); the lane report H-RX.md.
